descriptor: HVDC reactors, instrument transformers and grid power electronics
lede: A Sangli maker of reactors and coils for HVDC and grid projects that tripled its revenue in a year by buying control of Mehru (instrument transformers) and Endoks (Turkish power electronics and battery storage). Q2 FY27 revenue was ₹285 Cr (+39%), the order book passed ₹2,000 Cr and both new plants have started, but management warned Q3 would be 'tough' at the standalone business, a ₹700 Cr share sale is due, a third of profit belongs to minority partners, and the stock still trades near 70x earnings.

short_version.text: Q2 FY27 revenue ₹285 Cr (company figure; ₹273 Cr on Screener) and profit after tax ₹63 Cr (+80%). Order book above ₹2,000 Cr excluding WS Insulators. The Sangli coil factory started on 20 Oct and the Turkey PCS plant is running, ahead of the December date given in May. FY27 guidance (about 20% growth, margin about 20%) was left unchanged and FY28 growth of at least about 50% repeated.

Endoks and Mehru are only 51% owned: about ₹121 Cr of FY26's ₹186 Cr profit belongs to Quality Power shareholders. The Joint MD says Q3 will be 'a kind of a tough time' at the standalone coil business while it moves between factories, about 60 customer audits run until roughly April, inventory has risen, and ₹300 Cr of the planned ₹700 Cr share sale is for working capital.
About 70x trailing earnings and about 49x EV/EBITDA on Screener's 6 Nov data (price ₹1,364, down from ₹1,649 on 6 Oct), against 34x for Voltamp and 33x for Transformers & Rectifiers as of 6 Oct.

blocks.text: Quality Power makes air-core reactors, coils and line traps used in HVDC links, FACTS and grid connections, mostly for global OEMs such as Hitachi Energy, Siemens and GE, and exports most of its output. Through 51% stakes it owns Mehru (high-voltage instrument transformers, supplying about one in two used in India) and Endoks in Turkey (STATCOMs, SVCs and now battery-storage power conversion systems). Sukrut (transformer components) is a 50% associate.

items.text: Coil products earn the highest margins: Quality Power EBIT 33% in FY26, orders booked above 25%.
Endoks ~32% EBITDA in Turkish lira terms; battery-storage converters start at 10-12% and should rise to 17-18% with volume.
Mehru 15% EBIT in FY26, guided to ~18%.

Insulators (WS) orders are booked at 20-25% EBIT after an 8.25% duty; Endoks' traditional power electronics about 25% but battery-storage converters (PCS) only 10-12%; Mehru would have delivered 22-23% but for the copper and oil cost rise.
IPO in February 2025; revenue from ₹183 Cr (FY22) to ₹947 Cr (FY26, Screener).
Bought 51% of Mehru (March 2025); Endoks consolidated as a 51% step-down subsidiary.

New Sangli coil factory (started 20 Oct 2026), a CTC magnet-wire line (4-5 months to qualify) and a PCS factory in Turkey (operating); acquiring Winwin (ex-WS) Insulators, completion still pending (the Nov deck gives ₹272 Cr, half cash and half shares).

blocks.text: Management has beaten its own guidance, left FY27 guidance unchanged on 2 Nov and holds an order book above ₹2,000 Cr in a scarce niche. The share price has fallen about 17% since 6 Oct while quarterly profit rose, so the multiple is lower than in the October version of this note, but the price still assumes FY28's 50% growth arrives on time, two new plants ramp smoothly, ₹700 Cr of new equity is absorbed and acquisitions keep paying off; a third of group profit also goes to minority partners. The margin for error is thin.
